neighbours.label: A noun naming a list-like run of several items, in code or prose: a list, array, vector, queue, series or collection (also List types and [] values in code). 'set' and 'bunch', compounds like 'playlist', nouns for a single thing or an amount, and the verb 'to list' stay quiet.
neighbours.short: list-like run of items (list, array, queue, series), code or prose
fire: She wrote a shopping list before heading to the market.
The function returns an array of user IDs sorted by date.
Push the new element onto the vector and resize it if needed.
Incoming requests wait in a queue until a worker is free.
The museum hosted a series of lectures on ancient Rome.
His collection of antique coins filled three cabinets.
Declare it as List<String> names = new ArrayList<>(); before the loop.
Initialize the variable with an empty [] and append results as they arrive.
quiet: She wrote down one item before heading to the market.
The function returns a single user ID chosen at random.
Increment the counter and stop when it reaches the limit.
Each request waits patiently until a worker is free.
The museum hosted one lecture on ancient Rome.
He kept a set of antique coins in three cabinets.
Declare it as String name = ""; before the loop.
Please list the results as they arrive in the log.
